notes: Draft 1 mission library. Edit freely. Keep missions short, concrete, and screen-to-world.

missions.title: Penny Bridge
missions.prompt: Build a bridge that can hold 10 pennies (or 10 rocks).
steps: Build something that spans a gap.
Test it with 1 penny at a time.
If it fails, change ONE thing and try again.
missions.siblingStation: Give littles a bin of blocks and a “build a tower” mission.

skills.forMax: This helps you think like an engineer and learn from mistakes!
skills.forParent: Builds: spatial reasoning, iterative problem-solving, persistence through failure, early physics intuition (load distribution).

missions.title: Marble Run (No Kit Needed)
missions.prompt: Make a ball track that goes from high to low without falling off.
materials: Cardboard strips OR paper towel tubes
steps: Test, then add one more piece.
missions.siblingStation: Tape a long paper strip to the floor and let littles roll cars down it.

skills.forMax: You're learning how things move and how to build step by step!
skills.forParent: Builds: systems thinking, gravity/force concepts, incremental design, cause-and-effect reasoning.

missions.title: Target Landing
missions.prompt: Create a target and practice landing beanbags/socks in it from 3 different spots.
steps: Move spots if it’s too easy/hard.
missions.siblingStation: Littles throw from the closest spot; praise effort, not score.

skills.forMax: This helps your body and brain work together to aim and adjust!
skills.forParent: Builds: hand-eye coordination, distance estimation, self-regulation (adjusting difficulty), gross motor control.

missions.title: Paper Airplane Lab
missions.prompt: Make 2 planes and test which one flies farther (then change one fold).
steps: Fold Plane A, fly it 3 times.
Fold Plane B, fly it 3 times.
Change ONE fold on the worse plane.
missions.siblingStation: Littles decorate planes with crayons/stickers.

skills.forMax: You're being a scientist—testing ideas and learning what works!
skills.forParent: Builds: experimental thinking, comparison skills, controlled variables, aerodynamics intuition, following directions.

missions.title: Tape Road City
missions.prompt: Make a road map on the floor and add 3 places (home, store, park).
steps: Name 3 places and park cars there.
Make a rule: stop at signs, drive slow, etc.
missions.siblingStation: Littles get 2 cars each and a “park only in spots” rule.

skills.forMax: You're making your own world and learning how maps work!
skills.forParent: Builds: spatial mapping, symbolic representation, rule-making, social play, vocabulary (places, directions).

missions.title: Sound Hunt: {{SOUND}}
missions.prompt: Find 5 things that start with {{SOUND}} (or contain {{SOUND}}).
steps: Optional: put a sticky note on each thing you found.
missions.siblingStation: Littles hunt colors: “Find 3 red things.”

skills.forMax: You're learning to hear sounds in words and find them everywhere!
skills.forParent: Builds: phonemic awareness, sound-letter connection, active recall, environmental print awareness.

missions.title: Chalk Sound Jumps
missions.prompt: Write a word and jump each sound.
steps: Parent writes a simple word (ex: map, sun, fish).
Say the word fast at the end.
missions.siblingStation: Littles jump to shapes you draw (circle, square, triangle).

skills.forMax: Your body helps your brain remember sounds!
skills.forParent: Builds: phoneme segmentation, body-kinesthetic memory, blending sounds, movement-integrated learning.

missions.title: Letter Tag
missions.prompt: Tape 6 letters around the room. Run to the one I call!
steps: Write 6 letters (include 2 from Max’s current lessons).
Call a letter; Max runs and touches it.
Bonus: call a sound instead of the letter name.
missions.siblingStation: Littles run to a color card you call.

skills.forMax: You're learning letters by moving your whole body!
skills.forParent: Builds: letter recognition, letter-sound association, rapid recall, gross motor integration.

missions.title: Rhyme Race
missions.prompt: Find or invent rhymes and do a movement for each one.
missions.siblingStation: Littles repeat the last word and do the movement too.

skills.forMax: You're learning that words can sound the same and that's fun!
skills.forParent: Builds: phonological awareness (rhyming), word families, creative thinking, movement-memory connection.

missions.title: Jump + Add
missions.prompt: Do jumps, then add the totals.
steps: Show it with fingers or objects.
missions.siblingStation: Littles just copy the jumps and count to 5.

skills.forMax: You're learning to add by moving your body!
skills.forParent: Builds: early addition concepts, number sense, embodied math, quantity comparison.

missions.title: Sticks: More / Less / Equal
missions.prompt: Collect sticks (or toys) and compare which pile has more.
steps: Which is more? Which is less? Are they equal?
If they're not equal, make them equal by moving items. If they're already equal, make one bigger than the other.
missions.siblingStation: Littles sort items by big/small into two piles.

skills.forMax: You're learning which pile has more, less, or the same!
skills.forParent: Builds: comparison skills, quantity relationships, one-to-one correspondence, equalizing sets.

missions.title: Number Line Stomp
missions.prompt: Make a number line and stomp the answer.
steps: Say the number you land on (if you go past 10, stop at 10).
missions.siblingStation: Littles hop on just 1–3.

skills.forMax: You're learning to count forward on a number line!
skills.forParent: Builds: number line concepts, addition as movement, sequential counting, spatial number representation.

missions.title: Throw + Count (Mini Data)
missions.prompt: Throw 10 times and make a tiny ‘graph’ with objects.
steps: Throw 10 times; count hits vs misses.
Make 2 block towers: hits and misses.
missions.siblingStation: Littles throw 3 times from close distance.

skills.forMax: You're learning to collect data and see patterns!
skills.forParent: Builds: data collection, comparison (taller/shorter), counting, early graphing concepts, persistence.

missions.title: Spot 3 Signs of Life
missions.prompt: Find 3 signs that an animal was here (tracks, holes, nests, chewed things).
steps: Find 1 sign and point to it.
missions.siblingStation: Littles hunt “something tiny, something smooth, something rough.”

skills.forMax: You're learning to notice clues that animals leave behind!
skills.forParent: Builds: observation skills, inference, scientific thinking, attention to detail, nature awareness.

missions.title: Texture Sort
missions.prompt: Collect 10 items and sort by texture.
missions.siblingStation: Littles make a ‘treasure pile’ and count to 5.

skills.forMax: You're learning to sort things by how they feel!
skills.forParent: Builds: classification skills, tactile discrimination, category creation, descriptive vocabulary.

missions.title: Color Quest
missions.prompt: Find something in each color: green, brown, gray, and one surprise color.
steps: Pick a surprise color and find it.
missions.siblingStation: Littles just do green + brown.

skills.forMax: You're learning to find colors in nature and pick your own challenge!
skills.forParent: Builds: color recognition, visual scanning, choice-making, nature observation.

missions.title: Build a Tiny Habitat
missions.prompt: Build a ‘home’ for a pretend bug (no animals involved).
steps: Test: can your bug get in/out?
missions.siblingStation: Littles collect sticks into a bucket and deliver them.

skills.forMax: You're learning what animals need to live and how to build it!
skills.forParent: Builds: habitat understanding, systems thinking (needs: shelter, food, access), design thinking, nature connection.

missions.title: Co-op Obstacle Course (3 Rules)
missions.prompt: Build an obstacle course with siblings and agree on 3 rules.
steps: Pick 3 rules (no pushing, take turns, hands to self).
missions.siblingStation: This IS the sibling activity; keep it short and restartable.

skills.forMax: You're learning to work together and make rules everyone agrees on!
skills.forParent: Builds: cooperation, rule-making, negotiation, turn-taking, sibling collaboration, self-regulation.

missions.title: Play Store
missions.prompt: Set up a store with 5 items and practice greetings + paying.
missions.siblingStation: Littles pick 1 item and practice 'thank you.'

skills.forMax: You're learning how stores work and how to be polite!
skills.forParent: Builds: social scripts, money concepts, role-play, politeness routines, perspective-taking.

missions.title: Helper Mission
missions.prompt: Do one real helper job with a clear finish line.
steps: Pick 1 job: wipe table, match socks, feed animals, water plants.
Set a finish line (2 minutes or 10 items).
missions.siblingStation: Littles do a mini-version: ‘put 5 toys in the bin.’

skills.forMax: You're learning to help your family and finish what you start!
skills.forParent: Builds: responsibility, task completion, contribution to household, executive function (finish line concept), pride in work.

missions.title: Money Mission
missions.prompt: Make 3 ‘items’ and pay for them with coins.
steps: Pick an item and pay exactly.
Switch roles and be the cashier.
missions.siblingStation: Littles ‘buy’ with buttons or blocks.

skills.forMax: You're learning how money works and how to pay for things!
skills.forParent: Builds: money concepts, counting coins, exact payment, trading/exchange, real-world math application.

missions.title: Earthquake Tower
missions.prompt: Build the tallest tower that can survive an ‘earthquake.’
materials: A cookie sheet or sturdy cardboard
steps: Rebuild with one new idea (wider base, triangles).
missions.siblingStation: Littles build a short tower and do a tiny shake.

skills.forMax: You're learning what makes things strong and stable!
skills.forParent: Builds: structural engineering concepts, stability principles, cause-and-effect (base width affects stability), resilience thinking.

missions.title: Float Test (Boat Builder)
missions.prompt: Build a boat that can hold 10 pennies without sinking.
steps: Float it and add pennies slowly.
If it sinks, change ONE thing (wider, taller sides).
missions.siblingStation: Littles do water play with cups nearby (separate bowl if needed).

skills.forMax: You're learning why some things float and others sink!
skills.forParent: Builds: buoyancy concepts, displacement understanding, iterative design, early physics (density, surface area).

missions.title: Spoon Catapult
missions.prompt: Build a launcher that can hit a target.
missions.siblingStation: Littles collect launched pom-poms into a bucket.

skills.forMax: You're learning about force, angles, and how to hit a target!
skills.forParent: Builds: trajectory concepts, angle/force relationships, precision practice, counting/data collection, mechanical thinking.

missions.title: Maze Maker
missions.prompt: Build a maze for a toy car and try to solve it.
steps: Change one wall to make it harder/easier.
missions.siblingStation: Littles get a ‘parking lot’ with 3 parking spaces.

skills.forMax: You're making puzzles and learning how to solve them!
skills.forParent: Builds: pathfinding logic, spatial problem-solving, perspective-taking (designer vs solver), difficulty calibration.

missions.title: Letter Sprint
missions.prompt: Run and touch the letter {{LETTER}} five times (fast + silly).
missions.siblingStation: Littles run to a smiley face card.

skills.forMax: You're learning letters by moving your whole body!
skills.forParent: Builds: letter recognition, letter-sound association, rapid recall, gross motor integration.

missions.title: Syllable March
missions.prompt: March the syllables in names and objects.
missions.siblingStation: Littles march too; keep words short.

skills.forMax: You're learning to break words into parts by marching!
skills.forParent: Builds: syllable awareness, phonological segmentation, body-kinesthetic memory, word structure understanding.

missions.title: 3-Sound Word Builder
missions.prompt: Build a 3-sound word with letter cards, then act it out.
materials: Paper letter cards OR fridge letters
missions.siblingStation: Littles match 3 letter cards that look the same.

skills.forMax: You're learning to build words and read them!
skills.forParent: Builds: phoneme-grapheme mapping, blending sounds, early reading, encoding (spelling), comprehension through acting.

missions.title: Shape Hunt
missions.prompt: Find 10 shapes in the house or outside.
missions.siblingStation: Littles find circles only.

skills.forMax: You're learning to spot shapes everywhere around you!
skills.forParent: Builds: shape recognition, pattern spotting, visual discrimination, environmental awareness.

missions.title: How Many? (Fast Eyes)
missions.prompt: Show a small group of objects for 2 seconds; guess how many.
missions.siblingStation: Littles count to 3 with you.

skills.forMax: You're training your eyes to see numbers fast!
skills.forParent: Builds: subitizing (instant quantity recognition), working memory, visual processing speed, number sense.

missions.title: Measure With Steps
missions.prompt: Measure 3 things using your feet/steps.
missions.siblingStation: Littles measure 1 thing and cheer.

skills.forMax: You're learning to measure things with your own body!
skills.forParent: Builds: measurement concepts, comparison (longest/shortest), non-standard units, spatial estimation.

missions.title: Nature Scavenger 5
missions.prompt: Find: something smooth, something rough, something pointy, something tiny, something that smells.
steps: Find each item and make a pile.
Swap one item for a better one.
missions.siblingStation: Littles find smooth + tiny.

skills.forMax: You're learning to notice textures and smells in nature!
skills.forParent: Builds: sensory awareness, descriptive vocabulary, observation skills, multi-sensory learning.

missions.title: Shadow Hunt
missions.prompt: Trace a shadow and come back later to see if it moved.
missions.siblingStation: Littles trace their hands with chalk.

skills.forMax: You're learning how shadows move and change!
skills.forParent: Builds: time concepts, sun movement understanding, observation over time, scientific thinking (change detection).

missions.title: Compliment Pass
missions.prompt: Pass an object; when you get it, say one kind sentence.
materials: A soft ball or stuffed animal
steps: Sit or stand in a circle.
Say one kind sentence to the next person.
Do 6 passes and stop while it’s fun.
missions.siblingStation: Littles can say ‘I like you’ or ‘thank you.’

skills.forMax: You're learning to say kind things to people!
skills.forParent: Builds: social-emotional skills, kindness practice, turn-taking, positive communication, emotional vocabulary.

missions.title: Laundry Sort Race
missions.prompt: Sort laundry by person or type as fast as you can (with a finish line).
missions.siblingStation: Littles match socks or put washcloths in a pile.

skills.forMax: You're learning to help your family and finish jobs!
skills.forParent: Builds: responsibility, categorization, completion skills, contribution to household, sorting/classification.

missions.title: Invent a Mission
missions.prompt: Make up your own challenge with 3 rules and a finish line.
steps: Pick a theme (cars, animals, ninjas, space).
Pick a finish line (time or task).
missions.siblingStation: Let littles choose one rule (like ‘no yelling’ or ‘crawl only’).

skills.forMax: You're learning to make up your own games and change the rules!
skills.forParent: Builds: creativity, autonomy, rule-making, flexible thinking, ownership of learning, executive function (planning).

missions.title: Rule Remix
missions.prompt: Pick any mission you've done before. Do it again, but halfway through change ONE rule.
steps: When you're halfway done, stop and change ONE rule.
missions.siblingStation: Littles watch and cheer when you change the rule.

skills.forMax: You're learning that rules can be changed and that's okay!
skills.forParent: Builds: flexible thinking, rule-bending creativity, sequence understanding (by reversing it), humor/playfulness.

missions.title: Backwards Mission
missions.prompt: Pick a build mission and do the steps in reverse order.
steps: Pick a build mission (bridge, tower, maze, etc.).
Read the steps backwards (last step first).
Do it backwards and see what happens.
If it's funny or weird, that's the point.
missions.siblingStation: Littles build normally and watch you do it backwards.

skills.forMax: You're learning that rules can be changed and that's okay!
skills.forParent: Builds: flexible thinking, rule-bending creativity, sequence understanding (by reversing it), humor/playfulness.

missions.title: Rhythm Repeat
missions.prompt: Clap a pattern; copy it; add one beat.
steps: Max adds ONE beat to the pattern.
missions.siblingStation: Littles just clap along (no pattern needed).

skills.forMax: You're learning patterns and making your own music!
skills.forParent: Builds: pattern recognition, rhythm awareness, auditory memory, creative expression, turn-taking.

missions.title: Syllable Stomp
missions.prompt: March syllables for 5 household objects.
missions.siblingStation: Littles march too and say 'stomp-stomp-stomp.'

skills.forMax: You're learning to break words into parts by marching!
skills.forParent: Builds: syllable awareness, phonological segmentation, body-kinesthetic memory, word structure understanding.

missions.title: Sound Orchestra
missions.prompt: Find 3 things that make different sounds; play them in order.
materials: 3 objects that make sounds (pots, spoons, boxes, etc.)
steps: Decide on an order (quiet → loud, or your choice).
missions.siblingStation: Littles get one 'instrument' and play along.

skills.forMax: You're learning to make music and put sounds in order!
skills.forParent: Builds: sound discrimination, sequencing, volume concepts (quiet/loud), creative expression, pattern-making.

missions.title: Ask-Wait-Trade
missions.prompt: Practice asking for a toy, waiting 5 seconds, then trading.
steps: Ask nicely: 'Can I have that toy?'
missions.siblingStation: This IS the sibling activity; practice with littles.

skills.forMax: You're learning to ask nicely, wait, and trade toys!
skills.forParent: Builds: social scripts, impulse control (waiting), negotiation skills, turn-taking, polite language.

missions.title: Helper Interview
missions.prompt: Ask a family member 3 questions and remember the answers.
steps: Ask 3 questions (ex: favorite color, favorite food, favorite game).
Tell someone else what you learned.
missions.siblingStation: Littles ask one question: 'What's your favorite color?'

skills.forMax: You're learning to ask questions and remember what people say!
skills.forParent: Builds: conversation skills, active listening, memory, perspective-taking, information gathering.

missions.title: Same or Different?
missions.prompt: Find 2 leaves (or rocks); list 3 ways they're the same and 3 ways they're different.
steps: Find 2 similar items (2 leaves or 2 rocks).
missions.siblingStation: Littles find 2 items and say 'same' or 'different' for each.

skills.forMax: You're learning to notice what's the same and what's different!
skills.forParent: Builds: comparison skills, classification, descriptive vocabulary, observation, analytical thinking.

missions.title: Change Detector
missions.prompt: Pick one spot outside; visit it 2 days in a row and notice what changed.
steps: Pick one spot (a tree, a patch of grass, a rock).
Mark it or take a photo (optional).
Come back tomorrow and see what changed.
missions.siblingStation: Littles help mark the spot with chalk or a stick.

skills.forMax: You're learning to notice how things change over time!
skills.forParent: Builds: observation over time, change detection, memory, scientific thinking, patience (waiting until tomorrow).

missions.title: Blend Builder
missions.prompt: Build words with consonant blends (bl, cr, st, etc.) using letter tiles; read each one and use it in a sentence.
materials: Letter tiles or cards (include blends: bl, cr, st, fl, tr, etc.)
steps: Build 3 words that start with that blend.
Use one word in a sentence.
missions.siblingStation: Littles match 2 letter cards that look the same.

skills.forMax: You're learning to read and use words with blends!
skills.forParent: Builds: consonant blend recognition, decoding, reading fluency, sentence building, vocabulary.

missions.title: Sight Word Spy
missions.prompt: Given 3 sight words, find them hidden around the house (written on cards placed by parent); read each one aloud and act it out.
steps: Find each card and read it aloud.
Act out the word (or use it in a sentence).
missions.siblingStation: Littles hunt for a color card you hide.

skills.forMax: You're learning to read sight words anywhere!
skills.forParent: Builds: sight word recognition, reading in context, movement-integrated recall, game-based practice.

missions.title: Word Family Flip
missions.prompt: Pick a word family (-at, -ig, -op); build 5+ words by swapping the first letter; race to read them all.
steps: Build 5 words by changing the first letter.
Time yourself: can you read all 5 in 10 seconds?
missions.siblingStation: Littles say the ending sound (-at, -at, -at).

skills.forMax: You're learning word families and reading faster!
skills.forParent: Builds: word family patterns, rapid decoding, phoneme substitution, reading fluency.

missions.title: Sentence Builder
missions.prompt: Given 4–5 word cards, arrange them into a sentence; read it; then scramble and rebuild.
materials: 4–5 word cards (e.g. The cat sat on the mat)
steps: Try a different order (silly sentences allowed).
missions.siblingStation: Littles put 2 cards in order.

skills.forMax: You're learning how words go together to make sentences!
skills.forParent: Builds: sentence structure, word order, reading comprehension, syntax awareness.

missions.title: Add to 20 Relay
missions.prompt: Physical relay where each station has an addition problem (using objects); solve it to advance.
materials: Small objects at each station (blocks, rocks)
steps: Set up 3 stations with objects and a problem at each.
Run to station 1; use objects to solve; say the answer.
Run to station 2; solve; say the answer.
Do it again with new problems.
missions.siblingStation: Littles run the relay and count objects at each station.

skills.forMax: You're learning to add to 20 while moving!
skills.forParent: Builds: addition within 20, movement-integrated math, object-based counting, fluency.

missions.title: Mystery Number
missions.prompt: "I'm thinking of a number. It's 3 more than 7. What is it?" — physical number line + deduction.
materials: Number line (0–20) on floor with chalk or sticky notes
steps: Parent gives a clue: "3 more than 7" or "2 less than 10."
Switch: you give a clue, parent finds it.
missions.siblingStation: Littles hop on just 1–5.

skills.forMax: You're learning to add and subtract in your head!
skills.forParent: Builds: mental math, number line reasoning, more/less than, deductive thinking.

missions.title: Shape Builder
missions.prompt: Build 2D shapes from sticks/straws; count sides and corners; combine shapes into a picture.
steps: Build a triangle. Count sides and corners.
Build a square. Count sides and corners.
Build a rectangle. Compare to the square.
Combine 2 shapes to make a picture (house, car, etc.).
missions.siblingStation: Littles make a circle with one stick (or trace a shape).

skills.forMax: You're learning shapes and how they fit together!
skills.forParent: Builds: 2D shape recognition, sides and vertices, composition, geometry vocabulary.

missions.title: Coin Counter
missions.prompt: Real coins; "Can you make 15 cents three different ways?"
steps: Make that amount one way. Put it in bowl 1.
Make it a different way. Put it in bowl 2.
Make it a third way. Put it in bowl 3.
missions.siblingStation: Littles sort coins by type (big/small).

skills.forMax: You're learning how coins add up!
skills.forParent: Builds: coin values, equivalent amounts, counting money, flexible thinking.

missions.title: Stack 3
missions.prompt: Stack 3 blocks (or cups) as high as you can.
missions.siblingStation: Same activity—everyone stacks.

skills.forMax: You're learning to balance and build!
skills.forParent: Builds: fine motor control, hand-eye coordination, cause-and-effect, persistence.

missions.title: Balls in the Basket
missions.prompt: Put 5 balls (or rolled socks) into a basket.
steps: Put the basket on the floor.
Pick up one ball and drop it in.
Do it again with the rest.
Dump them out and do it again!
missions.siblingStation: Same activity—take turns or use two baskets.

skills.forMax: You're learning to aim and let go!
skills.forParent: Builds: hand-eye coordination, object permanence, counting, repetition.

missions.title: Clap With Me
missions.prompt: Clap to the beat of a nursery rhyme or song.
steps: Sing or say a short rhyme (e.g. "Pat-a-cake").
Do it again, faster or slower.
missions.siblingStation: Everyone claps together.

skills.forMax: You're learning rhythm and sounds!
skills.forParent: Builds: phonological awareness, rhythm, imitation, turn-taking.

missions.title: Point to It
missions.prompt: When I say a word, point to that thing.
missions.siblingStation: Use colors: "Point to red."

skills.forMax: You're learning that words mean things!
skills.forParent: Builds: receptive vocabulary, word-object association, listening, joint attention.

missions.title: Count to 3
missions.prompt: Count 3 things together: 1, 2, 3.
steps: Do it again. Let toddler try.
missions.siblingStation: Same—count together.

skills.forMax: You're learning numbers!
skills.forParent: Builds: one-to-one correspondence, number names, quantity sense.

missions.title: Big and Small
missions.prompt: Find something big and something small.
missions.siblingStation: Everyone finds big and small.

skills.forMax: You're learning big and small!
skills.forParent: Builds: size comparison, vocabulary, observation, comparison.

missions.title: Touch a Leaf
missions.prompt: Go outside and touch one leaf.
materials: Outside (or a leaf you bring in)
steps: Go outside (or hold up a leaf).
missions.siblingStation: Everyone touches a leaf.

skills.forMax: You're learning about nature!
skills.forParent: Builds: sensory exploration, nature connection, vocabulary, observation.

missions.title: Find Green
missions.prompt: Find something green outside (or in the room).
steps: When toddler points or picks: "Yes! Green!"
missions.siblingStation: Find red, then blue.

skills.forMax: You're learning colors in nature!
skills.forParent: Builds: color recognition, observation, vocabulary, outdoor time.

missions.title: Hand It Over
missions.prompt: Hand a toy to someone and say "Here!"
materials: A person to give it to
steps: Other person says "Thank you!" and gives it back.
missions.siblingStation: Pass a ball around the circle.

skills.forMax: You're learning to share and give!
skills.forParent: Builds: social scripts, turn-taking, giving, reciprocity.

missions.title: High Five
missions.prompt: Give 3 people a high five.
steps: Say: "High five!" and hold up your hand.
Do it with the next person.
missions.siblingStation: Everyone gets a high five.

skills.forMax: You're learning to connect with people!
skills.forParent: Builds: social connection, imitation, motor planning, celebration.

missions.title: Toys in the Bin
missions.prompt: Put 3 toys in the bin.
steps: Point to 3 toys on the floor.
Toddler puts them in (help if needed).
missions.siblingStation: Everyone puts 3 in.

skills.forMax: You're learning to help!
skills.forParent: Builds: task completion, contribution, following directions, pride in work.

missions.title: Wipe the Table
missions.prompt: Wipe the table with a cloth.
missions.siblingStation: Give littles a dry cloth to "clean" a toy.

skills.forMax: You're learning to help our family!
skills.forParent: Builds: practical life skills, contribution, imitation, motor skills.

missions.title: Sky Writing: {{LETTER}}
missions.prompt: Write a giant {{LETTER}} in the air, then on someone's back, then with one finger on the table.
steps: Grown-up writes {{LETTER}} big in the air first. Watch where it starts.
Stand up. Write it in the sky with your whole arm, 3 times. Say each stroke out loud.
Write it on a partner's back. They guess the letter.
Write it small on the table with one finger.
missions.siblingStation: Littles draw big circles and lines in the air.

skills.forMax: You're teaching your arm the path of the letter, so your pencil knows it later!
skills.forParent: Builds: letter formation from the shoulder down, start point and stroke order, big-to-small motor control.

missions.title: Chalk Letter Road
missions.prompt: Draw giant chalk letters, then drive a toy car along each one, starting at the green dot.
steps: Pick 3 letters from Joyce's writing card this week.
Draw each one huge. Put a green dot where it starts.
Drive the car from the green dot along the letter, the way the pencil goes.
Hard mode: draw it again, smaller, with your eyes on the green dot.
missions.siblingStation: Littles drive cars on a big chalk circle and a straight road.

skills.forMax: You're learning where each letter starts and which way it goes!
skills.forParent: Builds: letter formation through movement, directionality, visual tracking, gross-to-fine transfer.

missions.title: Salt Tray Letters
missions.prompt: Write letters with one finger in a tray of salt, then shake it smooth and go again.
materials: A baking tray or shallow box
steps: Pour a thin layer of salt in the tray.
Write c, o, a, d, g. They all start like c.
Shake the tray smooth after each one.
Grown-up says a letter, you write it without looking at a model.
missions.siblingStation: Littles draw lines, circles, and their first letter in the salt.

skills.forMax: You're writing letters from memory, just like a real writer!
skills.forParent: Builds: independent letter recall (not tracing), formation families, tactile feedback, low-pressure practice.

missions.title: Shrink Ray
missions.prompt: Write one letter giant, then zap it with the shrink ray: medium, small, and tiny.
steps: Write a letter giant, as big as your hand.
Zap! Write it again, half as big.
Zap! Write it small enough to fit inside a box on your writing paper.
Zap! Can you make one tiny but still right?
missions.siblingStation: Littles draw a big circle, then a smaller circle inside it.

skills.forMax: You're learning to make your letters any size you want!
skills.forParent: Builds: size control (Max's letters run much bigger than the lines), motor planning, self-monitoring.

missions.title: Label Your Build
missions.prompt: Make a sign for something you built: its name, in your own writing.
materials: An index card or sticky note
steps: Choose a name for your build (1 to 3 words).
Say the sounds. Grown-up helps with spelling if you ask.
Write the sign. Leave a finger space between words.
Tape it on your build and give someone the tour.
missions.siblingStation: Littles draw a picture sign for their own build.

skills.forMax: You're writing for real, so everyone knows what you made!
skills.forParent: Builds: purposeful writing, spelling by sound, word spacing, pride in work.

missions.title: Trainer Team List
missions.prompt: Write your Pokémon team: 3 names, copied from your handbook.
steps: Find each name in the handbook.
Copy each name on its own line. Check: do the letters stay in the lines?
Draw a Poké Ball next to each one.
missions.siblingStation: Littles draw their favorite Pokémon and write its first letter.

skills.forMax: You're making a real trainer roster in your own handwriting!
skills.forParent: Builds: copywork with a purpose, letter size on lines, attention to detail, interest-driven practice.

missions.title: Mail Carrier
missions.prompt: Write a little note to someone in the family and deliver it.
steps: Write To and their name, then one short message (like I like you or Come play).
Draw a picture and write your name at the bottom.
Deliver it. Bonus: wait for a reply.
missions.siblingStation: Littles draw a picture card and scribble their name.

skills.forMax: You're sending real mail that someone gets to read!
skills.forParent: Builds: writing to communicate, names and short words, spacing, social connection.

missions.title: Brick Bank: Trade 10 for a Tower
missions.prompt: Build numbers with LEGO or Duplo: towers of 10 are tens, single bricks are ones. When you have 10 loose bricks, trade them for a tower!
materials: About 40 small bricks (LEGO, Duplo, or snap cubes)
Paper with two boxes: Tens | Ones
steps: Grown-up shows one first: snap 10 bricks into a tower. 'This tower is one ten.'
Roll the dice and add that many single bricks to the Ones box.
Got 10 or more ones? Snap 10 together and move the tower to Tens.
Say your number: '2 towers and 3 bricks is 23.'
First to 50 wins. Bonus: write the number each turn.
missions.siblingStation: Littles snap bricks into towers of 5 and count them.

twists.easier: Use one die and stop at 30.
twists.harder: Start at 50 and take bricks away. Break a tower when you run out of ones.

skills.forMax: You're the bank! Ten loose bricks always trade for one tower.
skills.forParent: Builds: place value, regrouping (carrying) with a concrete model before paper. Pairs with Joyce's regrouping lesson: same idea, real objects.

missions.title: Quarter Shop
missions.prompt: Open a shop where everything costs 25 cents. Shoppers have to pay with different coins each time.
materials: Real coins: pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters
steps: Write 25¢ on a sticky note for each toy.
Shopper 2 pays with dimes and nickels only.
Shopper 3 pays with nickels only. How many does it take?
Shopkeeper counts every payment out loud before handing over the toy.
missions.siblingStation: Littles are shoppers: they hand over a quarter and get a toy.

twists.easier: Price everything at 10¢ and use dimes, nickels, and pennies.
twists.harder: Price things at 35¢ or 50¢ and give change from a dollar.

skills.forMax: You're the shopkeeper. Make sure every shopper paid exactly 25 cents!
skills.forParent: Builds: nickel, dime, and quarter values; equal amounts made different ways; skip counting by 5s and 10s.

missions.title: Clock Detective
missions.prompt: Use a real clock to figure out how many hours until something fun happens today.
materials: A clock with hands (a toy clock or paper plate clock works)
Today's plan: lunch, rest, dinner, bedtime
steps: Set the clock to now (round to the hour).
Move the hour hand one hour at a time. Jump or clap each hour.
Do 3 events. Which one is the longest wait?
missions.siblingStation: Littles hold up a finger for every clap.

twists.harder: Go backwards: 'We had breakfast at 8. How many hours ago was that?'

skills.forMax: Detectives count the hours to crack the case!
skills.forParent: Builds: elapsed time in whole hours (his current AdaptedMind edge), reading an analog clock, counting on.

missions.title: Inch, Foot, or Yard?
missions.prompt: Guess the best unit first, then measure to check: inches for little things, feet for medium things, yards for long things.
materials: A ruler (1 foot) and a yardstick or string cut to 1 yard
6 things to measure (a crayon, a book, a chair, the couch, the hallway, a toy car)
steps: Hold up the ruler: 'This is one foot. The tiny marks are inches.'
Pick a thing. Guess first: inch, foot, or yard?
If the number got really big or really tiny, try a different unit.
Line the things up from shortest to longest.
missions.siblingStation: Littles find something longer than their arm and something shorter.

twists.easier: Just sort things into 'smaller than the ruler' and 'bigger than the ruler.'
twists.harder: Measure the hallway in feet AND yards. Why is the yard number smaller?

skills.forMax: Pick the right tool for the job, like a real builder!
skills.forParent: Builds: customary units and choosing the best unit for a length (flagged for a recheck on AdaptedMind), estimating.

missions.title: Vowel Team Treasure Hunt
missions.prompt: Two vowels walk together! Find word cards hidden around the room and sort them by their vowel team.
materials: 12 sticky notes with words: rain, play, tail, day, feet, read, tree, beach, boat, snow, coat, grow
3 'team bases' on the floor: AI/AY, EE/EA, OA/OW
steps: Find one, read it out loud.
Run it to the right team base.
When all 12 are home, read each team's words fast.
missions.siblingStation: Littles carry the found notes and say 'Go team!'

twists.easier: Use only two teams (AI/AY and EE/EA) and 8 words.
twists.harder: Add a silly sentence: use 2 words from one team in one sentence.

skills.forMax: Vowel teams make one sound together. You're the coach putting them on the right team!
skills.forParent: Builds: vowel team decoding (current Reading.com scope), quick word reading, movement between reads.

missions.title: Grocery List Writer
missions.prompt: Write 3 things our family really needs from the store. Your list goes to the store with us!
materials: Paper with 3 big boxes or wide lines
The fridge and pantry to check
steps: Walk to the fridge and pantry. What are we out of?
Say the first word slowly. Write one sound at a time.
Draw a tiny picture next to each word.
Read your list to a grown-up, then stick it on the fridge.
missions.siblingStation: Littles draw one thing they want on the list.

twists.easier: Write just 1 word and draw the rest.

skills.forMax: Real writers write things people actually use!
skills.forParent: Builds: writing with a purpose, sounding out to spell, letter size in big boxes (handwriting is his weaker strand).

missions.title: B-D Bed Check
missions.prompt: Make a 'bed' with your hands to remember which way b and d face, then check letters around the house.
materials: 6 cards: b, d, b, d, p, b (or letter magnets)
steps: Make two thumbs-up and press your fists together. That's a bed! The left hand is b, the right hand is d.
Say 'b-b-bed' with the left hand and 'd-d-d' with the right.
Grown-up holds up a card. Make your bed and check which hand it matches.
Say the sound, then hop once.
missions.siblingStation: Littles make a 'bed' with their hands and lie their head on it.

twists.harder: Read short words: bed, dad, bad, dig, bib.

skills.forMax: Your hands always know which way b and d go!
skills.forParent: Builds: b/d reversal fix (Gabi's reading card starts with this reminder), letter-sound link, a self-check she can use anywhere.

missions.title: Pillow Slide Words
missions.prompt: Step on a pillow for each sound, then slide your feet together to say the word, like Otter Slide!
materials: 3 pillows or paper plates in a row
Word list: sun, map, pig, hop, bed, cat, fun, sit
steps: Step on one pillow for each sound and say it.
Slide back across all three, saying the sounds together faster and faster.
Swap: you say the sounds, grown-up slides.
missions.siblingStation: Littles jump on a pillow when they hear their name.

twists.easier: Two-sound words: up, at, in, on.
twists.harder: Put a letter card on each pillow and read the sounds yourself.

skills.forMax: Slide the sounds together and the word pops out!
skills.forParent: Builds: blending short-vowel CVC words (sliding is what gets Gabi to push sounds together), phonemic awareness.

missions.title: Snack Plate Adding
missions.prompt: Put some snacks on one plate and some on another. Slide them together. How many now?
materials: Up to 5 small snacks (crackers, grapes, cereal)
steps: Put 2 on one plate and 1 on the other.
Count each plate out loud, touching each snack.
Slide both plates into the bowl and count all of them.
Try new numbers. Never more than 5 total. Eat your answer!
missions.siblingStation: Littles drop snacks into the bowl one at a time while everyone counts.

twists.harder: Hide one plate under a napkin. 'There are 5 in all and 3 here. How many are hiding?'

skills.forMax: Two little groups make one bigger group. Yum!
skills.forParent: Builds: adding within 5 with real objects, one-to-one counting, the words 'and' and 'make.'

missions.title: Hop to 20
missions.prompt: Make a path of 20 spots and hop along it counting every hop.
materials: Chalk outside, or tape or paper plates inside
A marker to number the spots
steps: Make 20 spots in a line (grown-up writes the numbers).
Hop on each spot and say its number.
At 10, stop and do a big jump: 'Ten!'
Keep going to 20, then hop backwards to 1.
missions.siblingStation: Littles hop to 5 with a hand to hold.

twists.harder: Grown-up calls a number, you run to that spot.

skills.forMax: Your feet can count all the way to 20!
skills.forParent: Builds: counting to 20 in order, numeral recognition 1-20, teen numbers after the ten jump.

missions.title: Two-Step Helper
missions.prompt: Listen to two jobs, then do them both in order, like the game Two Jobs!
materials: Things around the house: a sock, a ball, a book, a cup
steps: Grown-up says two jobs: 'Touch the door, then bring me a sock.'
Hold up 1 finger for the first job and 2 fingers for the second.
Do them both, in that order.
Come back and say what you did: 'Door, then sock!'
missions.siblingStation: Big kids give the two-step jobs to the littles.

twists.harder: Three jobs: 'Clap, spin, then sit on the rug.'

skills.forMax: You remembered two whole jobs!
skills.forParent: Builds: listening, holding two directions in memory, sequencing (first/then). Matches Connor's Two Jobs game.

missions.title: Sock Match Count
missions.prompt: Find the sock partners in the laundry and count the pairs!
materials: A pile of clean socks (5 to 10 pairs)
steps: Dump the socks on the floor.
Pick one sock. Find its partner by color.
Put the pair in a row.
When all are matched, count the pairs together: '1, 2, 3...'
missions.siblingStation: Littles find all the socks of one color.

twists.easier: Only 3 pairs with very different colors.

skills.forMax: You're a sock detective, and the laundry helper too!
skills.forParent: Builds: color and pattern matching, one-to-one counting, a real household job.

missions.title: Fall Leaf Line-Up
missions.prompt: Collect fall leaves, then line them up from smallest to biggest.
steps: Go outside and collect 5 leaves of different sizes.
Find the tiniest one. Put it first.
Find the biggest one. Put it last.
Fill in the middle, then count the line together.
Bonus: sort them by color (red, yellow, brown).
missions.siblingStation: Littles crunch leaves and say each leaf's color.

twists.easier: Just find one big leaf and one little leaf.
twists.harder: Line up 10 leaves and say which number is the biggest one.

skills.forMax: Small, medium, BIG! You put them all in order.
skills.forParent: Builds: comparing size, ordering, counting, color words, outdoor movement.

missions.title: Color Basket Hunt
missions.prompt: Pick one color. Walk around and fill a basket with things that are that color.
materials: Toys and safe things around the house
steps: Pick a color together: red, blue, yellow, or green.
Walk around and find 3 things that color.
Put each one in the basket and say its color: 'Red ball!'
Dump them out and pick a new color.
missions.siblingStation: Big kids hide 3 things of the color for the littles to find.

twists.easier: Grown-up holds up two things: 'Which one is red?'
twists.harder: Find things of two colors and sort them into two piles.

skills.forMax: You found all the colors!
skills.forParent: Builds: color names (Ethan's focus), matching, following a simple direction, walking while looking.

missions.title: Table Setter
missions.prompt: Set the table for a real meal: one plate, one cup, and one spoon for every person.
materials: Plates, cups, and spoons (unbreakable is fine)
steps: Count how many people are eating.
Put one plate at every seat.
Put one cup by every plate, then one spoon.
Check: does every plate have a cup and a spoon?
missions.siblingStation: Littles carry napkins and put one on each plate.

twists.harder: Add a name card at every seat. Write or trace each name.

skills.forMax: Everyone's spot is ready because of you!
skills.forParent: Builds: one-to-one correspondence, counting a set, a real family job with a clear finish.

missions.title: Thankful Tower
missions.prompt: Take turns adding a block to one family tower. Every block is something you're thankful for!
steps: Sit in a circle around the building spot.
On your turn, say one thing you're thankful for and add a block.
Wait for the next person: listen to what they say.
Keep going until the tower falls or reaches 20 blocks. Count them!
missions.siblingStation: Littles add a block and say one word, like 'Mama' or 'dog.'

twists.easier: Everyone just names a favorite thing.
twists.harder: Say who you're thankful for and why.

skills.forMax: A tower full of good things, built by the whole family.
skills.forParent: Builds: turn-taking, listening to others, gratitude language (Thanksgiving week), counting the finished tower.
